rival_explanations: short-run financial gains (short-term performance improvement) as the cause of the market's positive revaluation of divesting firms

data_sources.name: corporate level accounting data (requisite accounting data)

analyses.label: Table 1. Financial ratios for divesting and non-divesting firms, before and after divestment (n=68)

dv.name: firm financial performance (profitability, liquidity, leverage)
dv.measure: four accounting ratios measured before and after divestment: Current ratio; Return on total assets = net profit after taxes / total assets; Debt to total assets = total debt / total assets; Times interest earned
dv.source: corporate level accounting data (requisite accounting data)

key_ivs.name: divestment status (divesting vs non-divesting firm)
key_ivs.measure: 68 voluntary divestments by Fortune 500 firms announced in the Wall Street Journal 1976-79 vs a matched control set of non-divesting counterpart firms

analyses.label: Table 2. Financial data disaggregated by divestment type (strategic, tactical, distress)
analyses.sample: 68 divesting firms disaggregated by divestment type (strategic / tactical / distress) and their matched counterpart firms

dv.name: firm financial performance (profitability, liquidity, leverage)
dv.measure: same four accounting ratios (Current ratio; Return on total assets; Debt to total assets; Times interest earned) before and after divestment
dv.source: corporate level accounting data (requisite accounting data)

key_ivs.name: divestment type
key_ivs.measure: divestment classified as 'strategic', 'tactical', or 'distress' (classification identified by Montgomery et al.)

key_ivs.name: divestment status (divesting vs non-divesting firm)
key_ivs.measure: divesting firms within each type compared with their matched non-divesting counterpart firms
